<meta>continues from previous page</meta>tigate; for the proper work of **Cold** is **Condensation**; and it is accomplished without any malignancy or hostile quality: and therefore the operation is safer than through **Opiates**; although a little less powerful, if it were used only at intervals as **Opiates** are: but again, because it can be used familiarly and moderately in the daily diet, it is even far more powerful for the prolongation of life than through **Opiates**.

**History of Life and Death.** 227

<margin>39</margin> The **Cooling of the Spirits** is done in three ways; either through **Respiration**; or through **Vapors**; or through **Foods**: the first is best, but almost outside our power; the second is also powerful, and yet is at hand; the third is weak and through a circuitous route.

**Air** <note>Catchword for the following page.</note>

<summary>Bacon argues that cold is a safer method than opium for thickening the vital spirits because it lacks harmful qualities and can be integrated into daily life. He identifies breathing, vapors, and diet as the three primary ways to cool the spirits.</summary>
<keywords>cold, condensation, cooling of the spirits, respiration, vapors, diet, prolongation of life</keywords>
